Subject: Follow-up: residency controls & contingency options

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the demo today. A few items came up on our side that we need clarified before we take this to Security & Legal:

- Primary ask: can we pin customer traffic (and any persistent logs) to a single country in the US region and guarantee no cross-border replication by default?
- Escape hatch: if the pinned region experiences an outage, what are our options? We need a clear failover policy that both preserves PII controls and gives us an acceptable RTO/RPO.
- Backups & snapshots: where are backups stored, are they replicated cross-region, and what encryption/KMS controls apply?
- Logging: retention window for audit logs, redaction of PII in logs, and granularity of access audits.

I've attached our initial questionnaire (medsys-residency-questionnaire.xlsx) — Sarah (Security) put the items in there. Can you send a short technical statement we can share with Legal that outlines: 1) default behavior, 2) configurability (manual vs automatic failover), 3) expected RPO/RTO for warm-standby, and 4) whether cross-border copies exist for backups/snapshots?

Appreciate a concise reply. If useful we can schedule a technical deep-dive next week.

Thanks,

Head of Product Security
MedSys Health

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — great questions. Below is a short, shareable summary you can pass to Legal + Security. I also copied Hannah (infra) and Neha (compliance) so they can add technical/contractual notes.

1) Default behavior and pinning- By default our hosted offering places all customer data and operational logs in the region selected at onboarding. For "US" residency we pin to US-based zones (US-East or US-West depending on customer preference). No automatic cross-border replication of primary data happens unless the customer opts in via contract or admin setting.

2) Escape hatch / failover options- Manual failover: the default for residency-sensitive customers — failover requires a customer/admin trigger (no automatic cross-border failover).- Automatic warm-standby: optional and available — we maintain a warm-standby in a secondary region (for example EU) for capacity and DR. Warm-standby can be configured to: 1) receive only encrypted snapshots (no live persistent copies of PII unless explicitly enabled), or 2) accept live traffic in emergency only.

3) RPO/RTO guidance (high-level)- Logs & metadata: typical async replication RPO is under 15 minutes; RTO to bring warm-standby to accepting traffic is typically targeted at 30–45 minutes depending on model footprint and KV cache size.- Persistent customer storage: if you require zero cross-border copies, we can provide manual-only failover with cold snapshots retained in-region.

4) Backups, encryption & KMS- Backups are encrypted at rest with customer-shared KMS or Redwood-managed keys. By default snapshots are stored in the pinned region. Cross-region snapshots are only created when warm-standby or geo-replication is enabled. We support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for additional control.

5) Logging & retention- Default audit/log retention: 90 days for request/response logs and operational traces. PII redaction: PII can be redacted from logs via configurable filters; we provide an opt-in PII-scrubbing pipeline and field-level redaction for high-sensitivity customers. Extended retention and export for audits can be added contractually.

Next steps (proposed):
- Hannah and Neha to prepare a short ops-runbook that outlines the activation flow (manual vs automatic), KMS options, and sample RTO/RPO tests (target: by Tue 06 Oct).
- Schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive with your infra/security leads (suggest Wed 07 Oct or Thu 08 Oct).
- I can also provide a redlined paragraph you can share with Legal to lock down cross-border replication behavior in the contract.

Attachments I will share: redwood-ops-runbook-stub.pdf, sso-kms-overview.pptx.

Would you like us to make failover manual-only by default for your account while we iterate on warm-standby options?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear summary. Couple of clarifying items from our infra team:

- How are snapshot restore operations audited? We need a chain-of-custody log for restores and access to who performed them.
- For RPO: 15 minutes for logs is OK, but what about the model cache and ephemeral session state — will that be lost on failover?

Our Legal also asked for a single-paragraph statement we can include in the SOW that says: "MedSys data will be pinned to US-based infrastructure and will not be automatically replicated outside the US without explicit written consent from MedSys."

Can you provide that language?

MedSys Health

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: residency controls & contingency options

Tom / Sarah —

Quick answers from infra:
- KMS scoping: yes — when using customer-managed keys we can restrict key usage to a specific region/region-tenant and configure the keys such that snapshot decryption requires access that is limited by policy to US-based operators. We will document the key policy for Legal.
- Restore auditing: all snapshot restore operations generate an auditable event with: operator id, timestamp, object id, pre/post-checksum and the activation playbook id. Events are stored in the pinned region and can be exported for your SOC ops.
- Model cache / session state: ephemeral KV cache is local to the serving pool and is not guaranteed to survive failover. In warm-standby mode we replicate model artifacts and persistent metadata; session-level KV will be rehydrated over time and therefore short-lived sessions may lose in-flight context.

Additional notes:
- If you require zero chance of cross-border snapshots, we recommend: manual-only failover + customer-managed KMS + contract clause restricting replication. This gives the cleanest compliance posture but increases recovery time.
- We will prepare a short ops-runbook with activation steps, example audit events, and a sample SOW paragraph by Tue 06 Oct.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
